column3: Judgement Comment: "Infants will be centrally randomised to either the experimental or control group with a 1:1 allocation ratio at the Copenhagen Trial Unit using a web-based randomisation application."
column5:
Judgement Comment: "The allocation sequence will be computer-generated with varying block sizes concealed
for all investigators, as the web-based program will not release the randomisation until the patient has been included in the trial and stratified by NICU and gestational age group (lower gestational age (< 26 weeks) compared to higher gestational age (≥ 26 weeks)."
column7: Judgement Comment: "Due to the nature of the experimental intervention, it is not possible to blind the clinical staff, the infant, or the parents to study group allocation."
column9:
Judgement Comment: "The outcome death was not blinded. Severe brain injury was performed in a blinded fashion but there was no central adjudication of cerebral ultrasound images. However, the diagnosis and classification of brain injury along with the entry of these data into the patient report form was conducted by an assessor blinded to study group allocation.
The data managers, statisticians, and those drawing conclusions were blinded to study group allocation. Assessments of other exploratory outcomes were not blinded."
column11:
Judgement Comment: "Withdrawal of patients was described: "The parents of 18 infants who were enrolled under the terms of deferred consent did not eventually provide written informed consent and declined the use of
their infants’ data. For three infants who were enrolled under the terms of prior informed con-
sent, the parents withdrew their consent and, for two of the three infants, also withdrew consent
for the use of their infants’ data. Two infants from one site were lost to follow-up because
the site withdrew from the trial shortly after the start of data collection"
The potential influence of missing data was assessed: " The results of the best–worst and worst–best case analyses and multiple imputation analyses showed that missing data did not have the potential to substantively affect results."
Nonadherence to the assigned intervention was described: "Nonadherence to the assigned intervention was documented in 36 of 772 infants (4.7%) in the oximetry group (who each had more than 14 hours of missing oximetry monitoring data) and in 20 of 807 infants (2.5%) in the usual-care
group (who underwent oximetry monitoring)""
column13:
Judgement Comment: "The trial was analysed in accordance with a pre-specified plan.
Statistical analyses were conducted independently by two of the authors. The results of the
analyses were compared for discrepancies before unblinding; no significant discrepancies were
found.
All outcomes will be assessed at 36 weeks postmenstrual age: this assessment and data entry will be conducted by a person blinded to group allocation."

column15:
Judgement Comment: "The eight centres contributed 6, 8, 9, 11, 21, 36, 36, and 39 participants. The intervention effect showed significant heterogeneity amongst the centres (P<0.001). Removal of one centre with 36 infants resulted in the heterogeneity being insignificant (P=0.62). This centre had the largest reduction in
burden in the intervention group. A post hoc sensitivity analysis reducing the mean effect of the intervention in this centre to a value equal to the mean effect in the rest of the centres resulted
in a significant reduction in burden of 31% (P=0.0497)."
